mbm-0718.clue: I keep the channel dial on my blanket.
mbm-0718.quote: The knob came off our old television years ago. In my pajamas under the blanket I can decide the next channel without even standing up. Somebody still has to go put the knob back on.

mbm-0719.clue: I make a leather loop for every key.
mbm-0719.quote: I cut a narrow leather loop for our shed key so Dad could find it by feel. Then I made a wide one for the gate. He can open the whole garden in the dark.

mbm-0720.clue: I practice high notes on the fire escape.
mbm-0720.quote: The first robin of spring answered me from the tree. We traded three notes before it got bored. I went back inside with a much better ending for my song.

mbm-0721.clue: I look at the frames in the portrait hall.
mbm-0721.quote: One frame has a tiny carved pear at each corner. The museum attendant noticed me sketching them and showed me a second frame with plums. We went fruit picking for an hour without leaving the building.

mbm-0722.clue: I saved the red squares for the lights.
mbm-0722.quote: My quilt is a view across the harbor at night. At the very end I added three little red cabin lights. My brother named the boats beneath them before I'd even tied off the thread.

mbm-0723.clue: I save my game on the ugly screen.
mbm-0723.quote: My adventure game has a perfectly peaceful clearing with one very ugly yellow chair. I save there after every difficult level. After six months that chair looks positively welcoming.

mbm-0724.clue: I read the same page to two audiences.
mbm-0724.quote: My twin nephews like different voices for the same pirate. I do one gruff reading and one very polite one. Now both pirates swap manners halfway down the page and the boys correct each other.

mbm-0725.clue: I quilt beside the drying dishes.
mbm-0725.quote: When the rack is empty, its little slots hold my folded blocks upright. Mum reached for a plate one morning and found a row of red pinwheels. I haven't been allowed to waste a washing-up turn since.

mbm-0726.clue: I stitched the shadow under the bridge.
mbm-0726.quote: My town quilt had houses and a river but the bridge kept floating off the fabric. A strip of purple under the arch fixed it. My sister says she can hear footsteps crossing now.

mbm-0727.clue: I keep chalk in a crooked little bag.
mbm-0727.quote: My kid brother sewed the chalk bag and attached the loop sideways. It swings around when I climb. I can find the opening without looking because it's always tapping the same hip.

mbm-0728.clue: I entered the corn round for the plate.
mbm-0728.quote: The fair gave each contestant a yellow plate shaped like an ear of corn. I finished somewhere in the middle, asked very politely, and carried my trophy home clean. We use it for toast.

mbm-0729.clue: I leave a secret in the quilt label.
mbm-0729.quote: Before I sew it down I tuck in a thread from the first seam. My mother taught me that. When I repaired one of hers, a little bit of the beginning fell into my lap.

mbm-0730.clue: I listen for the bamboo to fill.
mbm-0730.quote: A bamboo spout beside my favorite onsen tips into a little stone basin. I try to guess the next knock with my eyes closed. The water wins every time I start thinking in seconds.

mbm-0731.clue: I learned bocce on a sloping lawn.
mbm-0731.quote: My grandfather said the hill was playing too. You had to roll uphill and let it have a turn. On a level court I still glance over my shoulder for our old opponent.

mbm-0732.clue: I log the weather with each call.
mbm-0732.quote: I spoke to a radio operator one valley over while both our roofs were dripping. His rain stopped first. Six minutes later sunlight hit my logbook. That's the best forecast I've ever had.

mbm-0733.clue: I paddle to the floating garden.
mbm-0733.quote: Water lilies have taken over an old mooring float. I keep my kayak just far enough away to see all the flowers. One morning a turtle turned the whole yellow patch on like a lamp.

mbm-0734.clue: I stamp the moon into my leather.
mbm-0734.quote: My maker's mark is a little crescent from a dented washer. Press it one way and it's a moon, the other way a sleepy smile. I decide which after I know who's getting the wallet.

mbm-0735.clue: I sunbathe with half a crossword.
mbm-0735.quote: My friend tears the paper in two and we take one half each to the beach. Whenever the sun sends us to the shade, we trade clues and discover what the other half meant.

mbm-0736.clue: I bowl the red bocce balls first.
mbm-0736.quote: My mother used to say the red ones could see the little white pallino better. I explained why that was impossible, then lost to her eleven to two. Red it is.

mbm-0737.clue: I keep a notebook for our house rules.
mbm-0737.quote: Our game group awards an extra turn if a wooden goat falls on its feet. It's happened exactly twice. I recorded both landings in the margins, complete with witnesses.

mbm-0738.clue: I pack a clothespin for the tent door.
mbm-0738.quote: Our tent's flap kept falling across the sunrise. I pinned it up with a clothespin from my mother's washing line. Now the first light comes straight across the kettle and onto my pillow.

mbm-0739.clue: I programmed the tiniest tide pool.
mbm-0739.quote: My first little simulation had three pixel crabs and one rock. The crabs all crowded behind it. I gave them a second rock and spent the evening watching them ignore it together.

mbm-0740.clue: I sleeve my least powerful card first.
mbm-0740.quote: The little mushroom merchant can't win a battle. He was the first card anybody traded me, though, and his silver cap catches the light when I shuffle. Every deck needs somebody minding the shop.

mbm-0741.clue: I shop for the missing lid.
mbm-0741.quote: I bought a blue enamel pot without a lid and kept its outline on a scrap of paper. Three markets later a vendor laid a yellow lid on my drawing. Dinner's been two colors ever since.

mbm-0742.clue: I learned to ski on the other side of the wake.
mbm-0742.quote: My coach said my left turn looked like a question mark. She rode in the boat and drew the shape in the air. On my next pass she drew a long clean curve and whooped.
